messages:
jen_martin: Hey team, noticed a few DB snapshot objects in the backup bucket showing no SSE/CMEK headers when I pulled head-object. This is from last night's backup run. Anyone changed the uploader role or IAM recently?
omar_khan: ugh, thanks for flagging. Do you have an example object key?
jen_martin: s3://redwood-backups/prod/db-snapshots/2026-03-22/part-0003.tar.gz
jen_martin: head-object returned: 
```
> ContentLength: 42392812
> ServerSideEncryption: 
> x-amz-meta-encrypted-by: 
> x-amz-meta-kms-key-id: 
```
omar_khan: that blank ServerSideEncryption is worrying. Could be the uploader failed to attach metadata, or the CMK grant wasn't present.
sarah_sec: @omar_khan and @dex_oncall can we treat this as an encryption-in-transit breach candidate? If objects were stored without SSE-C or CMEK then it's a clear compliance hit. Need triage steps. :warning:
dex_oncall: I'll start with audit logs for the backup task. On it.
encops-bot: [audit-log-search] query=service:backup-uploader AND time>=2026-03-22T00:00:00Z AND time<2026-03-23T00:00:00Z returned 243 events (uploader-v2, uploader-v2-legacy).
dex_oncall: Quick findings: uploader-v2 ran with service-account: backup-uploader@redwood-prod. IAM policy shows no recent changes in the last 30 days. But there is a new temporary grant issued to backup-uploader for kms:Encrypt via a principal grant token on 2026-03-22 01:10 UTC.
omar_khan: can you paste the grant details? Maybe the grant TTL expired mid-run and the uploader fell back to SSE-S3.
dex_oncall: grant-id: GRT-20260322-81a, principal: uploader-sa-prod, kms-key: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh, ttl: 2h, issued_at: 2026-03-22T01:10:05Z, expired_at: 2026-03-22T03:10:05Z. The backup job ran 02:30 - 04:00 UTC. So part of the run overlapped with grant expiration.
sarah_sec: that would explain missing CMEK headers after expiry. Are the objects encrypted with SSE-S3 or unencrypted?
jen_martin: head-object showed no ServerSideEncryption header at all which suggests the uploader skipped setting encryption metadata, not that S3 re-encrypted unencrypted data. Need to check upload logs for 4xx/5xx or fallback path.
alex_dbeng: uploader code has a fallback that if kms:Encrypt returns AccessDenied it will retry with no-CMEK but still SSE-S3. There's a bug in older client where SSE-S3 header isn't always written when using multipart uploads and the client aborted part-way.
omar_khan: timeline looks like: grant expired -> uploader got AccessDenied on Encrypt -> fallback path triggered -> multipart commit path didn't set metadata for some parts -> final object missing headers.
sarah_sec: action items: 1) identify all objects created during the overlap window. 2) run audit to see if any cleartext copies exist outside S3 (unlikely, but check ephemeral storage). 3) rotate grants and extend TTL to avoid future mid-run expirations. 4) patch uploader fallback to fail loudly (do not silently drop encryption headers).
jen_martin: I can produce a list of affected keys; starting a quick scan now. Will push CSV to #eng-security-private.
dex_oncall: I'm also collecting backup-uploader logs and multipart commit traces. Early grep shows a handful of multipart complete calls with response 200 but no x-amz-server-side-encryption in the final head-object.
encops-bot: [scan-result] affected_count=7, sample_keys=["prod/db-snapshots/2026-03-22/part-0003.tar.gz","prod/db-snapshots/2026-03-22/part-0006.tar.gz"]
alex_dbeng: If objects are SSE-S3 (server-side with Amazon-managed keys) we still meet basic encryption-at-rest controls but it's not CMEK. Can we confirm which is the case for each object?
jen_martin: so far head-object for 5 objects show completely empty encryption metadata, 2 show ServerSideEncryption: AES256 (SSE-S3).
sarah_sec: classify the 5 as high-priority compliance finds. We need to notify compliance and create a short incident report. @legal and @compliance should be looped in.
jen_martin: question: can we re-encrypt objects in-place to CMEK without re-upload? S3 supports copy-object with SSE-KMS header set, but that means a copy operation which will incur read/write and must be performed carefully to preserve immutability requirements.
alex_dbeng: correct, you can do s3 copy-object with --server-side-encryption aws:kms and --sse-kms-key-id <key>. We'll script it for affected keys. Need kms:Decrypt/Encrypt permissions for the account doing the copy.
dex_oncall: immediate mitigation: extend grant TTL policy so long-running backups get full coverage, and add a preflight check that verifies active KMS grants before multipart upload starts (fail fast).
omar_khan: and long-term: uploader should fail the backup job if it can't attach CMEK rather than silently fallback. Also add a post-upload head-object verification step in CI.
sarah_sec: OK, I'll create the incident ticket (ENC-2026-042) and add remediation steps + owner assignments. jen, dex, alex own the mitigation work.
jen_martin: starting copy-based re-encrypt for the 5 objects now, will report success/failure.
dex_oncall: copying 1/5 done, copy preserved size and metadata but note: copy time for large files is ~3-4 min each. throttling OK.
encops-bot: [incident-created] id=ENC-2026-042, severity=medium, owners=[jen_martin,dex_oncall,alex_dbeng], created_by=sarah_sec
sarah_sec: good job catching this early. After remediation we should run a scan across last 90 days to ensure no other runs hit the same gap. :thumbsup:
jen_martin: update: 3/5 re-encrypted successfully, 2 failed with AccessDenied on copy (likely missing kms:Encrypt for the copier role). tagging @infra-automation to add perms.
omar_khan: adding infra-automation ticket for perms; make copier role a long-lived job with stable KMS grants.
sarah_sec: we'll also add an alert if head-object returns no encryption headers for uploaded snapshots.
alex_dbeng: note for postmortem: consider making backup snapshots atomic (single-object upload) or ensure multipart commit always attaches final metadata.
jen_martin: thanks all — keeping thread updated as re-encrypt finishes.
